account:
Today I have kept morning office hours and visited the mill for the scheduled ten-o'clock grain inspection. The mill stall chest contained 74 hay bales and 108 emeralds. I saw no mill representative to explain the stocks, and did not find the baker when I looked inside the bakery. I have now returned home ahead of noon lunch; council letters at thirteen, tea at the neighbour's cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the great hall meeting at eighteen remain on my schedule.

The unusual business is a reported 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk 01 named the baker, builder, freight and innkeeper as present. Other townsfolk repeated similar words, but supplied no concrete description of a change. The neighbour explicitly cautioned that this was secondhand and unconfirmed. I have not personally seen any alteration to a bridge or port.

There is also bread-related coordination. Yesterday evening I heard the baker asking the builder how many loaves had reached the hall, where freight was, and about settling grain funding. This morning the neighbour said the baker, freight and innkeeper had been coordinating a bread order, but did not know its outcome. These reports might concern food supplies and transport for the innkeeper's community hospitality matter at eighteen in the great hall, but I cannot establish that connection. My updated appointment says I should attend alone with no preparation needed, and the secretary has promised to remind and escort me. That is the only confirmed purpose of the evening meeting available to me; the crossing report and the bread order's outcome still need clarification.
